Chandler Bing got his happy ending in FRIENDS. Matthew Perry never did in real life

The line between the actor and the character begins to blur when you find out that most of Chandler’s traits were not a performance but just a reflection of the man playing him.

Triya Gulati

31 October, 2026 08:00 am IST

1

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

File photo of Matthew Perry | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

C ould it be any more heartbreaking?

For generations of FRIENDS fans, Chandler Bing, played by Matthew Perry , was the man who could make an awkward silence into a punchline, an existential crisis into a sarcastic one-liner and a stumble into physical comedy.

He was that friend who always had something funny to say.

Show Full Article

But Netflix’s recently released docuseries, The One About Matthew Perry , makes it difficult to watch Chandler the same way again. I couldn’t help but wonder how much of that laughter was borrowed from a life that was hurting.

The line between the actor and the character begins to blur when you find out that most of Chandler’s traits were not a performance but just a reflection of the man playing him. Now, Chandler remains frozen in time, forever surrounded by the people who love him. But Perry is gone.

The similarities between the two are uncanny. Both grew up in broken families. Both had abandonment and commitment issues. Both learned early that humour could be a defence mechanism, a way to deflect attention from feelings they did not know how to articulate. Chandler made jokes when he was uncomfortable, when he was vulnerable, when he was afraid of being rejected. Perry, too, used comedy to navigate the world.

The One About Matthew Perry was a painful watch because Chandler’s evolution had always felt like a promise. Here was a man who could be frightened, insecure and emotionally awkward, yet still find a home in another person and a group of friends. The documentary tells that Perry, who gave so many people comfort, continued to struggle with his own.

Even Chandler’s changing appearance throughout the ten seasons of FRIENDS , when viewed alongside Perry’s struggles with addiction, gives a clearer picture. The weight gains, weight loss, the puffiness around his face, the changes that viewers noticed and discussed over the years were visible reminders that Perry was struggling internally.

While the world blames his dependency on substances or alcoholism, the hurt was something deeper. Just like Chandler, it was the childhood trauma that haunted Perry.

Also read: Tiger Shroff could have been India’s Karate Kid. Bollywood missed the chance

Matthew Perry’s greatest wish and biggest fear Perry’s experience as an ‘unaccompanied minor’ at just five years old became one of the most heartbreaking blueprints of his life. Detailed deeply in his memoir, Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing , this single memory captured the profound sense of abandonment and loneliness that followed him long before he ever stepped onto the set of FRIENDS .

The initial fame and money blurred the wound, but when it resurfaced, nothing could heal it.

Rome Shidanlu, Perry’s former girlfriend, whom he met while in recovery, described his romantic life as “intimacy was his greatest wish and biggest fear.” It could just as easily have been a line written for Chandler.

Yet Chandler got something Perry could never—the happy ending.

Chandler found Monica. He built a family. He learned, slowly and awkwardly, to grow out of his childhood trauma. His story offered the comforting possibility that a man could outgrow his defences, confront his fears and find a home where he no longer had to hide behind a joke.

Perry, who died in October 2023 at 54, did not get to live out the decades of ordinary happiness that Chandler found.

Hence, Perry was an unconventional hero. He was not perfect. He was a man who struggled, relapsed, tried again and spoke openly about the darkness that followed him. By pulling back the curtain on his own pain, he helped others recognise theirs. His honesty gave people the language, and sometimes the courage, to seek help and keep going.

So, yes, watching Chandler will now feel a little different.

I will still laugh at his jokes. But somewhere under the laughter, I will always wish the man who gave us Chandler Bing could have found a little more of that happiness for himself.

(Edited by Saptak Datta)

CAIRO, Oct 30 (Reuters) – The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said on Friday it had intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by Yemen’s Houthis over Saudi Arabia’s Medina region, but the Iran-aligned group denied carrying out any attack towards the kingdom.

Medina is home to one of Islam’s holiest sites and is visited by millions of Muslim pilgrims each year.

Cross-border attacks involving the Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government, and the Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa, have intensified amid the US-Israeli war on Iran, opening another front in the conflict.

Show Full Article

The Houthis have repeatedly denied targeting Mecca and Medina, Islam’s two holiest cities, rejecting previous Saudi-led coalition accusations that it had launched drones towards the cities.

(Reporting by Enas Alashray and Ahmed Tolba;)

Iran’s IRGC Navy says four tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz

31 October, 2026 02:30 am IST

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

DUBAI, Oct 30 (Reuters) – Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Friday that four oil tankers had caught fire and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, while attempting to use what it described as unauthorised routes, Iranian state media reported.

In its latest statement, the IRGC Navy said a fourth vessel, a tanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil, had hit a mine, suffered a powerful explosion and was burning.

An IRGC Navy statement had said earlier that one of the tankers, which was also carrying 2 million barrels of crude oil, had hit a naval mine.

Show Full Article

Reuters was unable to immediately verify the statement.

Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said it had received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. A verified source told the agency that a crude oil tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while completing an outbound transit of the waterway.

Earlier, UKMTO said it had received a report that a vessel was hit by an unknown projectile on its port side about 40 nautical miles (74 km) south of Iran’s Lavan Island, causing a fire on board. The crew were reported safe and there was no reported environmental impact, it said.

Lavan Island lies in the Gulf, off Iran’s southern coast. It was not immediately clear whether the vessels cited by UKMTO were among the four tankers referred to by the IRGC Navy.

Tensions have persisted in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway through which around one-fifth of global oil supplies pass, since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran at the end of February.

State media said Iranian forces also downed and captured an MQM-170 US drone over Iran’s Qeshm island near the Strait of Hormuz. There was no immediate reaction from the US military and Reuters could not independently verify the report.

Iran also said it had destroyed an unmanned US vessel in the eastern Strait of Hormuz.

But the US military’s Central Command denied this and said in a statement on X: “All U.S. military unmanned surface vessels in the Middle East are accounted for, including a squadron of advanced sea drones on patrol in the Strait of Hormuz.”

(Reporting by Yasmine Ghania, Ahmed Tolba and Enas Alashray, additional reporting by Dubai newsroom; Editing by Alex Richardson, Timothy Heritage, Chizu Nomiyama and Sanjeev Miglani)

Ex-India lobbyist Jason Miller, a Trump loyalist, aided Flávio Bolsonaro’s private jet escape to US

The long-term Trump ally lobbied for India between April 2025 & June 2026. WSJ reported Miller helped charter jet used by the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate to reach US.

Keshav Padmanabhan

30 October, 2026 06:51 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro disembarks from the plane after arriving at Opa-locka Executive Airport near Miami, Florida on 28 2026. Inset Ex-India lobbyist Jason Miller. | Reuters. | X/@JasonMiller

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Jason Miller, a Trump-loyalist who lobbied for India till June this year in the US, aided in hiring the private jet that carried Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro from Argentina to Florida after he lost the poll, a result he strongly contested.

Miller joined the US government in July this year as a “special government employee” and worked with Eduardo Bolsonaro, Flávio’s brother, to hire a private aircraft to fly the defeated presidential candidate to Miami, according to a report by the Wall Street Journal (WSJ). Miller’s contract with the Indian Embassy was terminated on 23 June 2026, according to Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) disclosures.

Miller worked with President Donald Trump’s campaign almost a decade ago, and was slated to become the White House Communications Director until a controversy led him exiting the 2016 Presidential transition team. Miller has worked in all three Trump campaigns.

Show Full Article

In April 2025, the Embassy of India in Washington hired Miller and his firm SHW Partners LLC for a year-long contract worth $1.8 million. The contract was signed two days after the Pahalgam terror attack that left 26 people dead in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.

The contract with Miller was renewed earlier this year, with the payment terms remaining the same, as per disclosures made public under the FARA. Another firm signed up by the Indian Embassy in Washington—Mercury Public Affairs LLC—with links to Trump’s Chief of Staff Susie Wiles continues to lobby on behalf of the mission in the American capital.

As a special government employee, Miller can work for the US government for not more than 130 days in the last 365 days, the same limitations that were placed on Elon Musk last year, when he effectively headed the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) after Trump assumed power at the White House.

As a lobbyist for India, Miller spoke to a number of senior Trump officials, especially US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, amidst the ongoing negotiations for a bilateral trade deal between New Delhi and Washington, as per FARA filings.

Greer is the main negotiator for the trade deal on the US’ side.

Between November 2025 and April 2026, Miller disclosed at least eight calls with Greer, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, Wiles and Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick. India and the US announced the framework for a trade deal following a call between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Trump.

Miller’s close links with Trump, including previous communications work in all three presidential campaigns, made him a key lobbyist link to the White House. In his present role as a special government employee, Miller is reported by CNN to be responsible for crafting messaging to promote the accomplishments of the Trump White House.

As a part of Trump’s inner circle, Miller is reported to have also worked on Flávio’s exit from Brazil. Flávio, the son of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro, lost the presidential elections held on 25 October to Lula da Silva, the incumbent leftist President of Brazil.

A number of countries including India have recognised Lula’s victory.

Since arriving in Miami, Flávio has declared himself the legitimate leader of Brazil, raising questions over the Brazilian electoral process. He has found little support within Brazil or from his allies.

Flávio took aim at the extension of voting period by two hours, ordered by a Judge considered to be close to Lula as proof of electoral malpractice.

However, the younger Bolsonaro himself had requested an extension, which finds no mention in his latest statements. The night of the results, the Brazilian Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passport.

In an operation involving four vehicles, Bolsonaro and his family departed the Brazilian capital of Brasilia for Argentina less than 24 hours after losing the election, according to the WSJ .

He crossed the border into Argentina around 10 PM Tuesday, before departing on a private chartered aircraft from the border city of Puerto Iguazú around 12:21 am Wednesday before landing in Ecuador, according to the American newspaper.

Later Wednesday, Bolsonaro eventually reached Miami. The private aircraft was chartered with Baires Fly, according to WSJ , by Miller and Bolsonaro’s brother Eduardo who continues to live in Texas.

Flávio’s choice of leaving Brazil mirrors his father’s actions in the aftermath of the 2022 election defeat . The Bolsonaro senior left Brazil for Orlando, in Florida and remained in the US for around three months. The elder Bolsonaro refused to concede to Lula as well.

Eventually, the elder Bolsonaro returned to Brazil and was later convicted of attempting to overthrow the results of the 2022 elections. Jair (71) remains under house arrest.

Miller’s reported role in Flávio’s flight from Brazil, highlights the links of individuals to Trump’s inner-circle and why countries hire lobbyists linked to the American President. Lobbying is legal in the US, as long as all agents are registered under FARA and disclosures as required by law are filed.

(Edited by Ajeet Tiwari)
